narrativeLeft: Alpha FC is an athletic club based in Pereira, founded in 2020 by Jorge Esteban Suárez and Andrea González Londoño. The club uses fútbol sala (soccer played on smaller, indoor-style courts) to help children and teens build physical skills alongside personal character.

Un Sueño Que Construye Sueños (A Dream That Builds Dreams) is a program co-designed with Powerful Children Colombia. Children receive equipment, uniforms, and regular training, along with support from a psychologist and nutritionist. Parents take part in their own sessions to bring that same support home.
narrativeRight: Since its first phase in 2023, the program has grown and adapted based on where it's seen the strongest community engagement. Today, it reaches nearly 200 children across five communities: Taparcal, Acacias, Málaga, Normandía, and Santa Rosa de Cabal, with more than 80% of participants staying engaged throughout, and families reporting positive changes at home. Some participants have gone on to represent their communities in regional and national competitions.
This latest phase also introduces Juventud con Futuro, a new track for teens ages 15 to 17 to help them explore their goals and next steps as they approach adulthood.

narrativeLeft: Caminos Nativos is a Colombian-led organization based in Santander, founded in 2017 by Paola Arenas Duarte. Its work centers on social, cultural, and entrepreneurial projects that give children, adolescents, and women in rural, under-resourced communities new ways to spend their time, new possibilities for their future, and a stronger connection to their cultural roots.
narrativeRight: One of its programs, Pedalea con Conciencia (Pedal with Conscience), is a mountain biking program in Cabrera, Santander. Since 2022, children have received bikes and ongoing coaching from a professional cyclist and a child psychologist. The same two people have been with the program since day one and have built real trust with the kids and their families. Participation requires staying enrolled in school.
Since launching in 2022, the program has supported stronger academic performance, closer family relationships, and better physical and emotional well-being among its participants.

items.name: Más Que Vencedores
items.summary: Más allá del tablero (Beyond the Chessboard) is a pilot chess program that reaches 100 children across five public schools in Santa Marta.
items.tagline: Every move builds sharper minds and steadier hearts.

narrativeLeft: Fundación Más Que Vencedores (MQV) is an organization based in Santa Marta, Magdalena, founded in 2018 by Fernando Pavón in the Gaira neighborhood, starting with ten kids and one chessboard. Of note, Fernando is the leader of the Chess League of Magdalena and is certified by the Colombian Federation of Chess. The organization reaches approximately 150 children annually.

MQV's belief that chess can teach kids far more than checkmates anchors its mission: using the game to build strategic thinking and emotional resilience in children living in some of Santa Marta's most vulnerable communities.
narrativeRight: Más allá del tablero (Beyond the Chessboard) is a program that launched July 2026, in five public schools across Santa Marta: Nuestra Señora de Fátima, Liceo del Norte, Bastidas, El Pando, and Francisco de Paula Santander. Over four months, it will reach 100 children ages 8 to 17, at least a third of them girls, through three sequential levels of chess instruction (basic, intermediate, advanced), each lasting about 40 days.

Every session pairs 30 minutes of emotional and psychosocial development with 30 minutes of technical chess instruction and an hour of supervised practice matches, building toward biweekly training tournaments and a closing tournament.
